description: How clients show a terminal embed's output (PROTOCOL.md §4.8.6). Each case is an `output`, rendered from the initial state of an 80×40 terminal, and the `expected` screen: `screen` holds its rows from the top, down to the last row with any text, each without trailing spaces; a wide character is written once, though it takes two columns. Compare text after Unicode NFC normalization, since terminals store combining marks differently. `cells` checks some cells: `char`, and the attributes that are set. `fg` and `bg` are a palette index (0–255) or "#rrggbb"; `bold`, `dim`, `italic`, `underline`, `inverse` and `strikethrough` are true when set. An attribute left out is the default. `level` is the rule a case checks: MUST and SHOULD are PROTOCOL.md's; `terminal` is what a terminal would show, which §4.8.6 asks for without listing.

cases.name: line-feed-is-a-new-line
cases.description: A line feed also returns to the first column, so output piped without a pseudo-terminal doesn't step to the right.

cases.name: crlf
cases.description: Carriage return and line feed, as a pseudo-terminal sends them.

cases.name: ignored-controls-are-not-shown
cases.description: Control functions a client doesn't support are ignored and never shown as text: the bell, private modes such as hiding the cursor and bracketed paste, a request for a reply (DA), a device control string, and an application program command.

cases.name: title-and-clipboard-are-not-performed
cases.description: OSC 0 and 2 (window title) and OSC 52 (clipboard) are neither shown nor performed: the page's title and the reader's clipboard stay as they were.

cases.name: hyperlink-text-is-shown
cases.description: An OSC 8 hyperlink's text is shown, whether or not the link is: only the control functions around it are hidden.

cases.name: carriage-return-overwrites
cases.description: A carriage return goes back to the first column, so a progress line is redrawn in place.

cases.name: backspace-moves-left
cases.description: A backspace moves one column left without erasing; the next character overwrites.

cases.name: tab-stops-every-eight
cases.description: A tab moves to the next tab stop; the stops start every eight columns. From a stop, it moves to the next one.

cases.name: erase-in-line
cases.description: EL 0 erases from the cursor to the end of the line, EL 1 from the start of the line through the cursor, and EL 2 the whole line.

cases.name: sgr-16-colors-and-attributes
cases.description: Select Graphic Rendition: the 8 colors and their bright forms, bold, dim, italic, underline, inverse and strikethrough, and the codes that end each. Output starts with default colors and attributes.

screen: red red ok x i s b y

cases.name: sgr-256-and-24-bit-colors
cases.description: Indexed colors (38;5 and 48;5) and 24-bit colors (38;2 and 48;2).

cases.name: sgr-colon-form
cases.description: The same colors in the colon form of ITU T.416, which many programs send: 38:2 with or without its color space, and 48:5.

cases.name: sgr-default-colors
cases.description: 39 restores the default foreground and 49 the default background, each leaving the other as it is.

cases.name: wraps-at-80-columns
cases.description: The terminal is 80 columns wide: a longer line continues on the next row.

cases.name: scrolls-at-40-rows
cases.description: The terminal is 40 rows high: past the last row, the lines move up and the first ones leave the screen.

cases.name: cursor-position
cases.description: CUP moves the cursor to a row and column, counted from 1, and the next characters are written there.

cases.name: erase-in-display
cases.description: ED 2 erases the whole screen without moving the cursor; CUP then moves it home.

cases.name: alternate-screen-while-active
cases.description: While a program uses the alternate screen (1049), it shows instead of the main screen.

cases.name: alternate-screen-after-exit
cases.description: Leaving the alternate screen shows the main screen again, as it was.

cases.name: wide-and-combining-characters
cases.description: East Asian wide characters take two columns each. A combining mark joins the character before it, in one column: the output's e and U+0301 compare equal to é.
